newsitem.title: USA: UAL seeks to improve on-time flights, net.
newsitem.headline: UAL seeks to improve on-time flights, net.

text.p: UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, said it hopes to improve its on-time reliability record and its financial performance in 1997.
In 1996, UAL, which is majority owned by employees, earned a record $1.0 billion or $7.32 a share on a fully distributed basis, before extraordinary items.

In a letter to shareholders included in the annual report, UAL Chairan Gerald Greenwald and President John Edwardson said the company hopes to generate a fully distributed pre-tax margin in the top 20 percent of its peer group.

"Our strong performance in 1996 gives us the momentum to reach this objective in 1997 -- and it's one more step toward our longer-term goal to rank consistently in the top 10 percent," the executives said.
Regarding on-time performance, they said the goal is for 68 percent of departures to leave within five minutes of schedule, which would be a seven point improvement over 1996.
In the annual report, UAL reiterated that it expects the return of an investment-grade debt rating, but did not give a specific timeframe.
"And, although this is in the more distant future, we see an airline with the strength to provide some form of sharehodler dividend or stock repurchase program," the executives said.
